title: I Took the Chocolate-Temper Booking to the Chef Who Left My Numbered Marble

parts.text: I stepped into the temper bench at 9:09 a.m. and chef Yves was already using numbered gear. The board said: ONE MARBLE. FORTY-FIVE MINUTES. SEED STAYS WITH THE BOOKING. I was thirty, kitchen secretary, holding a clipboard that listed our numbered marble. Yves shrugged. "Chefs are the marble." I photographed the board, the booking, and his leftover seed on my numbered marble. Then I asked for the temper log. At 9:17 the bench pinged why Yves's name was on my seed. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The bench can see Yves's leftover seed on my numbered marble.

social.video_title: He left my numbered temper marble on my booking — Part 1/2
social.description: Temper bench, leftover seed, a forty-five-minute clock he posted. I logged the marble. Would you have asked for the temper log?

parts.text: Yves called it tabling until the bench asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the seed still. The marble went back to my numbered booking. Yves ran a slot of his own and told the next chef atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: CHEFS ARE NOT THE MARBLE. I keep my seed in a labeled tin. Yves brown-bags his tabling. The bench finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Chefs are not the marble — Part 2/2
social.description: Temper log, numbered marble, and a second line on the board. Was tabling ever my seed?
